subject: FS-job analysis (c6l ui60): FS jobs come from in-pass splits, not from pass count -> plan: one job per 2-attachment CA pass
body: Per backboardd command (1778 cmds): 5.87 passes (2.12 full-screen, 3.75 offscreen), 48 draws, 13.3 kernel jobs of which 9.24 full-screen (8.85 LOAD, 0.39 CLEAR). So a full-screen pass becomes ~4.4 jobs: the splits inside passes are memfetch 3.18 + mrt 3.72 + spans 0.39 per command (same_enc 7.48), while pass boundaries (target/new_enc ~4.8) are mostly offscreen. Pass merging alone can remove at most ~1 FS job/cmd (2.12 FS passes). Every CA pass has 2 colour attachments (att=0/369/0); 55 of the 64 logged pipelines write rt0 only, 8 write rt1 only; the 'mrt' jobs are true-MRT jobs (sidecar count>1) and the memfetch ones read an attachment through memory (tile path only covers 'input attachment == the draw's own rt'). The Mesa way, and what removes both splits: encode each 2-attachment pass as ONE job whose framebuffer has both RTs - every draw writes its RT(s) by render_target_mask, a fetch of either RT is an LD_TILE of that RT, LOAD preloads both RTs (pre-frame DCD writing 2 RTs), CLEAR clears per RT. Expected: FS jobs 9.2 -> ~2.1 per cmd (one per FS pass; ~1.5 with pass merging), GPU ~16.6 ms -> ~6-8 ms per cmd at 350 MHz (each split job today re-preloads and re-writes-back the touched tiles; estimate), plus ~5 ms/cmd less CPU (0.8 ms per kernel job outside the kernel). Split of work: bridge/n2r (mine): MRT LOAD (2-RT pre-frame preload), MRT batches (n2mb_batch_draw gains an optional render-targets pointer; per-draw RT mask/blends; shared 2-RT frame). Compile path (encode-cpu-opus): per-pipeline 'pass-MRT' variant = the pipeline compiled against the pass's full attachment list (outputs at their real locations, unwritten RTs masked, LD_TILE with rt index for any fetched attachment). Encoder: in a pass with >1 attachment, emit the MRT sidecar for every draw (targets = pass attachments with their load/clear) when the pass-MRT variant exists. Asking the encode agent to confirm the compile side; I start the bridge side now (host-testable). A device run with the new TEGU_BREAK_DETAIL lines would confirm the attachment roles (which pipelines are true MRT, which RT memfetch reads).
